source_issues.finding: Prose requires MCQ metric_name=exact_match, but LEGAL_CATEGORY_METRIC permits exact_match and accuracy. The code checks category/metric pairs, not category/post-process compatibility despite prose implying the latter.
Embedded few-shot prompt text is rejected by code only when heuristic markers exceed one AND few_shot_examples is absent/empty. Source describes unconditional rejection; retained.
extract_letter first searches for a standalone A-E letter, then falls back to the first A-E anywhere. The source says first matching character; e.g. Answer: C has A before C but code returns C.

Earlier prose says a bad line does not abort the run, later says runner refuses to start if errors exist absent --allow-bad-tasks. These can refer to validation vs model-running phases, but are not clarified in source. main.py has no such CLI flag; it is a demo entrypoint.

task_id is further limited to ASCII letters/digits/_/-; extract_code_block returns original text if no fence; extract_first_line strips surrounding whitespace. The 10 bad fixtures do not exercise every validation rule. These omitted/overbroad source claims were not expanded or fixed in translation.
